sections.title: Headline
sections.content: This month's notable papers span agentic geospatial reasoning, lab-in-the-loop molecular design, hardware-diverse AI training, and verification-driven or streaming agentic systems. Google, Meta, and Alibaba/Qwen each contribute work with verified affiliations.

sections.title: Google Earth AI Geospatial Reasoning Agent: Capabilities and a Systematic Evaluation
sections.problem: Answering complex geospatial questions requires combining data, foundation models, tools, and planning, but systematic evaluation of such agents is limited.
sections.method: Introduces GeoExpertQueries and GeoKTools and compares a standalone LLM, basic tools, GRA tools without upfront planning, and full GRA using Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemini 3.8 Flash.
sections.key_result: GRA performs well on templated and open-ended problems; domain tools and skills provide the largest gain, and planning further improves open-ended performance enough for Flash to match or exceed Pro at lower cost.
sections.caveat: Benchmark limitations include evolving ground truth and tool/data access differences.
sections.why_it_matters: Provides a systematic evaluation framework and shows that tools, skills, and planning can let a cheaper model match or exceed a stronger one on open-ended geospatial tasks.

sections.title: Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery
sections.problem: Tests whether LLM-based agents can improve biomolecular design through iterative wet-lab feedback.
sections.method: Three design-test-improve cycles for DNA aptamer binders to alpha-thrombin and myoglobin, with about 4,400 sequenced constructs.
sections.key_result: Bead-corrected on-target hit rates rose to 42.1% and 33.5% in round three; agents diagnosed cross-reactivity and changed strategies, restoring myoglobin specificity to 72.4%; orthogonal titrations agreed with pooled enrichment (Pearson r=0.90).
sections.caveat: Strictly de novo scaffolds remained low-micromolar binders, while preliminary nanomolar affinities involved literature-derived motifs; empirical lab feedback was more useful than computational proxies in this setting.
sections.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a closed-loop agentic discovery workflow where wet-lab feedback drives strategy changes, while carefully separating de novo from literature-derived performance.

sections.title: Architecting for Hardware Diversity: Meta's End-to-End Co-Design for High-Performance AI Training on AMD GPUs
sections.problem: Studies production training of recommendation models on AMD MI350X versus NVIDIA B200.
sections.method: Combines hardware-model co-design, Origami analytical kernel selection, and agentic workflows for kernel optimization and portability.
sections.key_result: Across production workloads MI350X reaches a geometric-mean throughput of 101% of the B200 baseline; compared with a directly ported baseline, the methods deliver up to 1.5x end-to-end throughput; Origami predicts optimal kernels with 93% accuracy.
sections.caveat: Remaining GEMM performance gaps and a focus on DLRMs rather than a full LLM-specific study.
sections.why_it_matters: Shows end-to-end co-design can make AMD GPUs competitive with NVIDIA for production recommendation-model training, while flagging remaining gaps and scope limits.

sections.title: ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation
sections.problem: Improving agentic image generation without updating the underlying generator.
sections.method: Keeps the generator frozen and combines five-dimensional verification and repair, a cross-task experience library admitted only after paired A/B validation, and offline judge updating with SFT and GRPO.
sections.key_result: On ImageReq-Bench (961 requests) reaches 65.66% Checklist Strict Accuracy, 9.28 percentage points above the strongest baseline; on MindBench reaches 52.6%, 10.2 points above the strongest baseline.
sections.caveat: Evaluation depends on checklist/judge quality and the benchmark setup, and the generator itself is not updated.
sections.why_it_matters: Shows verification-driven self-improvement can raise agentic image-generation accuracy while keeping the generator frozen, with explicit dependence on judge quality.

sections.title: SyncPro: Synchronous Reasoning and Responding for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding
sections.problem: Proactive streaming video understanding requires reasoning and responding to proceed concurrently.
sections.method: Dual-stream system with separate inner reasoning and user-facing response branches sharing causal history and activating independently; trained on 189K dual-stream examples using supervised fine-tuning and trajectory-level reinforcement learning.
sections.key_result: On StreamingBench achieves 41.2% accuracy within a two-second response window, 3.2 points above the strongest compared baseline; also reports gains on OVO-Bench and ProactiveVideoQA.
sections.caveat: Benchmark-specific evaluation and code not yet released at submission.
sections.why_it_matters: Introduces a concurrent reasoning-and-response architecture for proactive streaming video, with gains reported across multiple streaming benchmarks.

sections.title: Research Themes
content: Agentic systems with verification and iterative feedback loops
Tool use and planning as drivers of agent performance
Closed-loop integration of agents with external environments (geospatial tools, wet labs, hardware kernels)
Benchmark-specific evaluation with explicit caveats about ground truth and judge quality

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The selected papers center on agentic systems that improve through verification, planning, and external feedback rather than model updates alone. Google, Meta, and Alibaba/Qwen contributions all carry verified affiliations, and each paper states its own evaluation caveats. No temporal comparison is supported by the supplied metadata, so no portfolio shift is claimed.
